long_biography.plain_text:
Television producer Burt Sugarman paid for The Midnight Special's pilot when NBC declined to finance it. He recruited General Motors as a sponsor through John DeLorean, while Johnny Carson promoted the forthcoming broadcast. Paying for production allowed Sugarman to retain the programme, whose performances he later brought to new audiences online.

He insisted on live singing and turned away acts that would only mime. The running order was carefully judged: familiar singers appeared first to hold Carson's audience, with rock acts following as younger viewers stayed up. Behind the scenes, Wolfman Jack visited dressing rooms to reassure performers nervous about singing before television cameras.
